- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts show a gradual upward trend, while true outcomes often dip or show volatility, suggesting model fails to capture mean reversion or short-term corrections.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 90s to 95s), model continues upward trend, overshooting actual drop or plateau — indicates lag in recognizing market correction.
- Model underestimates volatility in late 30d window — true outcomes show sharper declines or sudden spikes (e.g., 90s → 80s or 80s → 95s) that model misses.
- Forecast mean is typically 3–5% higher than true mean — suggests persistent upward bias, possibly due to momentum or lagged data weighting.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonal or event-driven volatility — e.g., true outcomes show sharp drops after high peaks, model doesn’t reflect this.
- Forecasts often smooth out noise, leading to underestimation of short-term volatility or sudden reversals.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent highs” — forecasts rise with recent history, even when true outcomes show divergence or correction.
